arxiv-2512-21096.title: Identification with Orthogonal Basis Functions: Convergence Speed, Asymptotic Bias, and Rate-Optimal Pole Selection
arxiv-2512-21096.creator: Jiayun Li, Yiwen Lu, Yilin Mo, Jie Chen
arxiv-2512-21096.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jiayun Li, Yiwen Lu, Yilin Mo, Jie Chen. This paper is concerned with performance analysis and pole selection problem in identifying linear time-invariant (LTI) systems using orthogonal basis functions (OBFs), a system identification approach that consists of solving least-squares problems and selecting poles within the OBFs. Specifically, we analyze the convergence properties and asymptotic bias of the OBF algorithm, and propose a pole selection algorithm that robustly minimizes the worst-case identification bias, with the bias measured under the ℋ 2 \mathcal{H}_{2} error criterion.

pmc-13343779.description: Metastasis to the internal auditory canal (IAC) is rare, representing less than 1% of lesions in this region. pmc-13360835.title: Phosphoryl Radicals from Trivalent Iminyl Phosphines: A Photocatalytic Approach to N‐Phosphoryl Azetidines
pmc-13360835.creator: Chandu G Krishnan, Gabriel Cormier, Stefano A Serapian, Marco Bortolus, Luca Dell'Amico
pmc-13360835.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We report that iminyl phosphines, a class of bench‐stable and readily accessible trivalent P‐centered radical precursors, enable the synthesis of N‐phosphoryl azetidines via formation of a key phosphoryl radical under visible‐light single‐electron transfer (SET) catalysis. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SET oxidation of the iminyl phosphine engages a previously unexplored SET‐triggered polar pathway that channels the reaction away from classical phosphine oxidation toward the controlled generation of a P‐centered radical.
